factual_claims.source_evidence: Consolidated Statement of Comprehensive Income (page 19) shows net profit attributable to shareholders for 6M 2026 of EUR 12,843 thousand (12.8 million) vs 6M 2025 of EUR 21,676 thousand (21.7 million).

factual_claims.claim: The pre-tax margin fell to 7.2% from 14.0% and the net profit margin to 8.6% from 12.9%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Ratios table (page 10) shows 6M 2026 pre-tax margin of 7.2% vs 6M 2025 14.0%; net profit margin of 8.6% vs 12.9%.

factual_claims.claim: Second-quarter net profit was EUR 8.5 million, compared with EUR 11.2 million in the prior-year quarter.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Consolidated Statement of Comprehensive Income (page 19) shows Q2 2026 net profit of EUR 8,500 thousand (8.5 million) vs Q2 2025 of EUR 11,216 thousand (11.2 million).

factual_claims.claim: The construction services segment reported relatively stable six-month revenue of EUR 118.3 million, down 1.5%, but operating profit dropped 65.5% to EUR 3.0 million and its margin declined to 2.6% from 7.3%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Segment reporting table (page 23) shows construction service revenue for 6M 2026 of EUR 118,315 thousand (118.3 million) vs 6M 2025 EUR 120,094 thousand (120.1 million) - a 1.5% decrease; operating profit of EUR 3,042 thousand (3.0 million) vs EUR 8,808 thousand (8.8 million) - a 65.5% decrease; margin of 2.6% vs 7.3%.

factual_claims.claim: Management attributed the weaker margin primarily to the expiration of successful contracts from previous periods and a return to more typical margins in a highly competitive environment, with half-year results also affected by first-quarter seasonality.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Management Report (page 7) states: 'The operating profit margin was mainly impacted by the expiration of successful contracts highlighted in previous periods and a return to sector's more typical margins in a highly competitive environment, in half-year totals still affected by Q1 seasonality.'

factual_claims.claim: The real estate development segment's revenue fell 33.9% to EUR 31.6 million and operating profit declined 40.8% to EUR 7.0 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Segment reporting table (page 23) shows real estate development revenue for 6M 2026 of EUR 31,578 thousand (31.6 million) vs 6M 2025 EUR 47,788 thousand (47.8 million) - a 33.9% decrease; operating profit of EUR 7,021 thousand (7.0 million) vs EUR 11,862 thousand (11.9 million) - a 40.8% decrease.

factual_claims.claim: Apartment sales decreased to 120 from 222, while apartment-sale revenue fell to EUR 27.6 million from EUR 44.9 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Management Report (page 6) states: 'In 6 months 2026, the group sold a total of 120 apartments... in 6 months 2025, 222 apartments... The group earned a revenue of EUR 27.6 million... from sale of own developed apartments in 6 months 2026 and EUR 44.9 million in 6 months 2025.'

factual_claims.claim: Conditions improved sequentially in the second quarter, when 84 apartments were sold and development revenue reached EUR 22.6 million, compared with EUR 21.6 million a year earlier.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Management Report (page 6) states: 'In Q2 of 2026 a total of 84 apartments were sold... and earned a revenue of EUR 20.6 million from sale of own developed apartments (Q2 2025: EUR 20.2 million)'; Segment Reporting table (page 23) shows real estate development segment revenue for Q2 2026 of EUR 22,582 thousand (22.6 million) vs Q2 2025 EUR 21,614 thousand (21.6 million).

factual_claims.claim: The strongest positive development was the secured order book, which reached a record EUR 835.7 million at 30 June, up approximately 88% from EUR 443.8 million a year earlier.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Management Report (page 6) states: 'As of the end of the first half of the year, the group’s secured order-book reached an all-time high of EUR 836 million... As of 30 June 2026, the group’s secured order book was EUR 835.7 million (30 June 2025: EUR 443.8 million).' The increase is approximately 88%.

factual_claims.claim: New contracts signed during the half-year totaled EUR 486.4 million, compared with EUR 223.1 million in 2025.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Secured Order Book section (page 9) states: 'In 6 months 2026, EUR 486.4 million worth of new contracts were signed, which is EUR 263.3 million more compared to the same period of the previous year (6 months of 2025: EUR 223.1 million).'

factual_claims.claim: Major awards included the Krulli Quarter commercial building, event centre and infrastructure works in Tallinn.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Largest Construction Contracts table (page 9) lists contracts signed in Q2 2026: 'Construction contract for the construction of a commercial building named Kasvuhoone in Tallinn at Krulli Quarter... Construction contract for the construction of an event centre in Tallinn at Krulli Quarter... Construction contract for the construction of infrastructure in the Krulli Quarter in Tallinn.'

factual_claims.claim: The Rūdninkai defence campus project also entered full-scale construction in early July; its two phases have total construction costs exceeding EUR 370 million and are expected to contribute significantly to revenue in coming quarters.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Management Report (page 5) states: 'In early July, completed all preparatory stages required for the development of the Rūdninkai defence force campus project. The contract entered into full force, and construction activities have now commenced in full scale... The construction cost of the two phases exceeds 370 million euros in total, and the project’s contribution to revenue will increase significantly in the coming quarters.'

factual_claims.claim: Management reported increased activity in both segments during the second quarter, but also rising construction material and equipment prices, with no expected easing of price pressures.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Management Report (page 5) states: 'There was an increase in activity in both the construction services and development segment in the second quarter... The increase in construction input prices that anticipated in the first quarter has materialised, and there are currently no developments in the economy or global politics that would suggest any easing of price pressures.' Outlook section (page 7) also discusses persistent inflationary pressures.

factual_claims.claim: Public-sector, defence and Rail Baltica projects continued to support demand while private-sector customers remained cautious and price-sensitive.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Outlook section (page 7) states: 'The lack of private-sector orders and intense competition continue to leave the construction sector heavily dependent on public-sector and publicly funded projects... Orders for defence-related facilities remain high across all three Baltic states... Private sector clients still remain cautious, assessing profitability conservatively and viewing risks as high in the context of weak economic growth.'

factual_claims.claim: Cash and cash equivalents were EUR 39.6 million versus EUR 25.9 million, but operating cash flow worsened to negative EUR 31.6 million, mainly reflecting higher inventories and construction-contract balances.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Cash Flow Statement (page 21) shows cash and cash equivalents at 30 June 2026 of EUR 39,593 thousand (39.6 million) vs 30 June 2025 EUR 25,862 thousand (25.9 million); operating cash flow for 6M 2026 of EUR (31,602) thousand (-31.6 million). Notes to Cash Flow Statement explain: 'The negative effects to cash flow from operating activities came from the changes in receivables and liabilities related to construction contracts of EUR 15.1 million... from the change in inventories of EUR 24.1 million.'

factual_claims.claim: Additional development borrowing raised net debt to EUR 29.6 million and the debt ratio to 15.8% from 6.1%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Cash Flow Statement (page 21) and Ratios table (page 10) show net debt at 30 June 2026 of EUR 29.6 million (vs negative EUR 1.1 million at 30 June 2025); debt ratio of 15.8% (vs 6.1% at 30 June 2025). Management Report (page 9) notes: 'To support cash flows from operating activities, including increased volumes in apartment development, the group has raised additional external capital.'

factual_claims.claim: The company paid EUR 22.1 million in dividends, or EUR 1.25 per share.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Dividends and Dividend Policy section (page 14) states: 'On 28 April 2026, the shareholders of AS Merko Ehitus approved... to pay out the total amount of EUR 22.1 million (EUR 1.25 per share) as dividends from net profit brought forward... Comparable figures in 2025 were accordingly: EUR 33.6 million (EUR 1.90 per share) as dividends... for the year 2024.'
